newsitem.title: HAITI: Haiti prime minister nominee calls for economic reform.
newsitem.headline: Haiti prime minister nominee calls for economic reform.

text.p: President Rene Preval's choice as Haiti's new prime minister, Ericq Pierre, said on Friday his goal, if approved by parliament, would be to speed the overhaul of the economy.

"We need to move forward with economic reforms, and we need to do so at an accelerated rate," Pierre, 52, told reporters at his first news conference since his nomination. If approved, Pierre, Haiti's representative on the board of the Inter-American Development Bank, would succeed Rosny Smarth, another pro-business prime minister who resigned in June after months of sometimes violent street protests called to oppose the economic reforms.
Haiti's government wants to privatise nine state-run enterprises, including the telephone and electric companies, in hopes of attracting investment and new technology.

But opponents have criticised the plan as hurting Haiti's poor and risking its sovereignty. Many have already weighed in against Preval's choice of Pierre as prime minister. Besides his position at the IADB, Pierre has worked for the U.S. embassy and the U.S. Agency for International Development.
Pierre said he would look for compromise and negotiation with the anti-privatisation sectors.
"The economic programme is not the Bible," he said. "There is room for improvement in any programme."

Pierre declined to discuss who he might choose as members of his cabinet. In a process that could take weeks, he must put together a programme, present it to parliament and then be questioned by legislators before the approval vote.

Separately, USAID Administrator Brian Atwood left Haiti on Friday after signing agreements with Preval for $34 million in short term aid projects, including a $30 million agreement for food security and population control.
Atwood also expressed support for the government despite the months without a prime minister. "There is growing awareness this crisis is beginning to harm the people of Haiti," he said.
